verdict: SHIP, now measured on both sides. Typed access correctly resolves a field's type to another cross-file, Fields-attributed entity (Round A) and drives correct recursive dispatch in a generated 'describe' function (Round B). Round C (addendum, same day) built a real syntax-only resolver using Myriad's own Ast.fs matching code: it gets the unambiguous case right, then fails the adversarial one (two same-named records in different modules) in a measured, reproducible way - the identical resolver flips between correct and silently-wrong answers depending only on file processing order. Required BOTH Q001 pillars together (typed access AND whole-project in-process hosting) - Myriad's current per-file plugin invocation model (GeneratorContext.InputFilename, singular) would not reproduce this without also changing to a whole-project view. Output-side safety remains untested; Round B's own bug (unparenthesized nested call) is a live example of the failure class typed output would prevent.
